note: Hand-written weekly recaps, keyed league -> week number. Written every Tuesday from data/2026/week-NN.json; every number in a paragraph must trace to that file. Voice: Hall of Fame & Shame roast level -- punch at the decision, not the person. Real names in two_mitchs (config.json maps them), Sleeper handles everywhere else.

shape.headline: one line, the week in a sentence
shape.facts: optional array of 3-5 {k, v}; leave it out and the page builds the strip from the data
shape.paragraphs: array of strings, 2-3 paragraphs, about 300 words in all and 350 at most (the saved image fits one phone screen and shrinks the text to make long ones fit). **bold** and *italic* allowed, nothing else.
shape.epitaph: kings_justice only, optional: one roast line under 25 words about the team that died, shown on the Death Recap card and in its copy-paste text

1.headline: Puka's Bite Mark went into Monday night needing J.K. Dobbins. J.K. Dobbins had 3.6.
paragraphs: Eighteen in, seventeen out, and the first body belongs to **NickBova**. The warning came in the very first game of the season, when Romeo Doubs posted a clean 0.0, and it never got better. By the end of the Sunday early games NickBova sat at 51.16 with exactly one player left: J.K. Dobbins, on Monday night. Projected 10.04. Delivered 3.6. Final: 54.76 on a 110.45 projection, dead last by 18.88.

The one who should be sweating is **cbova1222**. After the late window it was *cbova1222* in the chop seat at 49.64, 1.52 behind the eventual corpse, courtesy of Jordan Addison's 0.0. Sunday night and Rashee Rice's 9.9 on Monday dragged Danger Zone to 73.64, which is 32.75 under projection and 17th of 18. Nobody survived anything. The axe just found a slower target.

At the top, **Elworth** put up 159.8 on a 112.41 projection behind 35.3 from Derrick Henry and takes the $25. Honorable mention to **avobttam**, the commissioner, who led the league at 123.8 after the early games, scored 3.4 points in the entire late window, and finished second by 4.8. The Executioner, everybody.

2.headline: bstanley45 sat in the chop seat after the 4:25 games. Then the Rams played Monday night.
paragraphs: Seventeen in, sixteen out, and the second body belongs to **Mpletcher**. By the end of the 4:25 window Mpletcher was finished: 53.02 on a 95.28 projection, zero players left, Colston Loveland contributing 1.3. The only hope was the man below. *bstanley45* sat in the chop seat at 38.7 with four players to go and needed less than 14.32 from all of them. They scored 128.78. Mpletcher spent Sunday night and Monday watching it happen.

The survivor who should be ashamed is **creckley**: 65.66 on a 95.45 projection, a 0.0 from RJ Harvey, and done after the 4:25 games, alive by 12.64 only because somebody was worse. Right behind, **Bustersx8** started Puka Nacua on Monday night, projected 0.0 and delivered exactly that, for 66.78. **DipLipGator** got -0.1 from DJ Moore and 0.8 from Jaxson Dart and finished 41.27 under projection at 69.0.

At the top, **bstanley45** went from the chop seat to the $25: 167.48 on a 97.14 projection, with Matthew Stafford (34.98) and Davante Adams (39.5) adding 74.48 on Monday night alone. **AllBidness** led the league after the 4:25 games on 42.5 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and 37.76 from Dak Prescott, had nobody left to play, and finished second by 3.82.

3.headline: AJPeak was done by 4:05 on Sunday. Bogeyman28 needed more than 5.46 from Jalen Hurts on Monday night, and got it.
paragraphs: Sixteen in, fifteen out, and the third body belongs to **AJPeak**. Kyle Pitts opened the week with 1.5 on Thursday night, and by the end of the 4:05 games AJPeak had nobody left and 70.66 on a 102.92 projection. Then came the wait. **Bogeyman28** sat in the chop seat after the 4:25 games at 57.6 with two players to go, and was still there after Sunday night at 65.2, with only Jalen Hurts left and 5.46 to find. Philadelphia lost 27-7 in Chicago. Hurts scored 12.62 anyway, and AJPeak went out by 7.16.

The survivor who should be embarrassed is **Bogeyman28**: 77.82 on a 102.31 projection, 1.8 from Brian Thomas, and a whole week riding on a quarterback whose team scored seven points. Hurts was projected for 19.98 and delivered 12.62, which was bad, and enough. Just above, **Bustersx8** was out of players after the 4:25 games at 86.18, and **CodyPowers28** sat in the chop seat after the 1:00 games at 28.26 with five players to go before climbing to 88.06.

The $25 goes to **cbova1222**, and it was a clean one: 133.16 on a 111.23 projection, 81.06 in the 1:00 games, 52.10 more at 4:05, and finished before the late games kicked off. **DipLipGator** led after the early window on Jahmyr Gibbs' 41.4, the best starter in the league, and finished second by 8.12. Commissioner **avobttam** was third at 124.7, 8.46 short of the money.

4.headline: Elworth was finished at 89.52 before Sunday night and needed one Monday collapse out of three. Atlanta and New Orleans scored 69 and nobody collapsed.
4.epitaph: Elworth died with all $1,000 unspent and 23.6 points on the bench, starting a receiver projected for zero.
paragraphs: Fifteen in, fourteen out, and the fourth body belongs to **Elworth**. Dalton Kincaid scored 1.7 in the 1:00 games, Ladd McConkey scored 0.0 at 4:25, and Elworth was out of players at 89.52 on a 102.58 projection before Sunday night kicked off. Then came the wait. Three teams went into Monday night below him, all with players in Atlanta's 45-24 win in New Orleans. **AllBidness** sat at 85.7 and needed 3.82 from Chris Olave. Commissioner **avobttam** sat at 86.3 and needed 3.22 from Tyler Shough and Devaughn Vele. **creckley** sat at 86.88 and needed 2.64 from Drake London. Olave scored 19.6, Shough and Vele scored 35.34 between them, and London scored 14.6. Not one of them came close.

The survivor who should be embarrassed is **humrich**: 91.26 on a 97.44 projection, alive by 1.74, a margin smaller than the 2.0 Saquon Barkley gave him. Kyren Williams scored 36.7, the third-best start in the league, and humrich still finished 14th of 15. Earlier in the day **creckley** held the chop seat after the 1:00 and 4:05 games at 31.08 and 32.88, and **DipLipGator** was in it after the 4:25 games at 52.5 with two players left, 0.22 behind Bogeyman28.

The $25 goes to **nelsolson**, and Monday night won it. CeeDee Lamb's 41.3 put him at 93.78 after the 1:00 games, but **joefanelli90** finished Sunday at 148.4 on an 86.52 projection, 61.88 over it, and nelsolson went into Monday 11.92 behind. Alvin Kamara, projected for 9.81, scored 22.8, and nelsolson took it at 159.28. **Bogeyman28** had the best start in the league, 45.2 from Tetairoa McMillan, and finished third at 135.52.

5.headline: The defending champion is dead. Bogeyman28 went into Monday night at 48.2, above a bstanley45 who had three Rams left. They scored 68.72.
5.epitaph: The defending champion spent $873 of $1,000 on a roster whose best possible lineup was 59.3, still 25.8 short of surviving.
paragraphs: Fourteen in, thirteen out, and the fifth body belongs to **Bogeyman28**, the 2025 champion. Brian Thomas opened the week with 0.0 on a 6.82 projection in the 9:30 game, Tetairoa McMillan, the $401 waiver claim, sat on the bench with no game, and Bogeyman28 finished Sunday night at 48.2 with only Keon Coleman left. That should have been enough. **cbova1222** held the chop seat after the 1:00 and 4:05 games at 19.2, and **bstanley45** took it after the 4:25 games at 28.6 and was still there after Sunday night, 19.6 behind. Then the Rams played Monday. They lost 37-34 to Buffalo, but Matthew Stafford scored 33.32, Davante Adams 22.1 and Tyler Higbee 13.3, and bstanley45 went from last to 97.32. Coleman scored 7.7. Bogeyman28 died at 55.9 on a 77.98 projection, and the best lineup on that roster was 59.3.

The survivor who should be embarrassed is **Cubbiesftw23**: 85.1 on a 116.58 projection, 31.48 under it, with 0.3 from Kenyon Sadiq, and 13th of 14. The margin was 29.2, and every point of it was Bogeyman28's doing.

The $25 goes to **Bustersx8**: 174.26 on a 121.16 projection. Drake Maye scored 47.46, the best start in the league, Bustersx8 finished the 1:00 games at 136.56 with only Puka Nacua left, and Puka added 37.7 on Monday night. **DipLipGator** was second at 157.98 on Jahmyr Gibbs' 37.7 and Jaylen Warren's 36.8, with a 0.0 from DJ Moore on Monday. Commissioner **avobttam** had zero points through the 9:30 game with all eight players to go, scored 121.2 in the 1:00 window, and finished fourth at 138.5.

6.headline: Cubbiesftw23 started a 0.0 tight end over 18.5 on the bench and got chopped by 17.12. Your Commish dropped 145.86 and took the $25. Obviously.
6.epitaph: Four seasons, one $25 check, and a career-best 13th, sealed by starting a 0.0 tight end with 18.5 on the bench.
paragraphs: Thirteen walked in, twelve walked out. **Cubbiesftw23**, you dumbass. You scraped by at 85.1 last week and celebrated by starting Juwan Johnson at tight end. Projected 11.07. Scored a goddamn 0.0. Colston Loveland sat on your bench and put up 18.5, and that one swap is worth more than the 17.12 you died by. You were out of players after the 4:25 games at 63.18 on a 115.82 projection, then spent Sunday night and Monday watching football like a fan. Bijan Robinson turned 25.16 projected into 7.3. Mahomes gave you 10.48. And the $427 Justin Jefferson sat on your bench projected for 0.0. Four hundred and twenty-seven dollars for a decorative fucking plant. The best lineup on that roster was 82.22. That lives. You had survival in your hands and you strangled it yourself.

But the real shitbird this week is **humrich**. 80.3 on a 99.85 projection, 12th of 13, and alive only because the guy below set himself on fire. **CodyPowers28** sat in the chop seat after the 1:00 and 4:05 games, 12.1 then 21.8, and had the decency to climb out to 84.3. You took the seat after the 4:25 games at 36.0 and were STILL in it after Sunday night at 53.0, 10.18 behind a corpse that was already done scoring. Your rescue squad was Jayden Daniels and Brandin Cooks, your $2 waiver claim. Cooks scored 2.3. Two dollars, flushed. Daniels dropped 25.0 on Monday night and dragged your sorry ass over the line. Don't thank Daniels. Thank Cubbiesftw23, who did most of the work keeping you alive.

And the $25 goes to... me. Of course it does. **avobttam**, The Executioner, 145.86 on a 115.46 projection, 30.4 over. I sat on a big fat zero through the 9:30 game with all eight guys still to play and you vultures thought I was cooked. By design. Tyler Shough dropped 32.96 and I put up 111.46 in the 1:00 window alone, then Christian McCaffrey tacked on 30.7 Monday night just to rub your faces in it. Last week I started just as slow and finished fourth. This week I got paid. One ring, 2024, won by 0.86 in the final, and now a weekly check. Legacy, baby. Fine: **nelsolson** was second at 134.88 behind C.J. Stroud's 28.98, and that is a legitimately great week, which makes me physically ill to type. Second pays nothing, you son of a bitch. The money's in my pocket.

7.headline: DipLipGator started Xavier Worthy's 4.1 over Tony Pollard's 36.5 and got chopped by 5.3. Your Commish took the $25 again. Back to back, baby.
7.epitaph: $740 of FAAB spent, $0 earned, and the 36.5 that would have saved DipLipGator sat on the bench behind a 4.1.
paragraphs: Twelve walked in, eleven walked out, and the body belongs to **DipLipGator**. First year in my league and you benched your own survival. Xavier Worthy started at flex and scored 4.1 on an 11.11 projection. Tony Pollard sat right behind him and dropped 36.5. That one swap is worth 32.4, more than six times the 5.3 you died by. Bryce Young gave you 7.42 on a 21.18 projection, which isn't a quarterback, it's a rumor. You had a 116.12 lineup sitting on that roster and rolled out 83.72 on a 126.69 projection, out of players after Sunday night, dead last of twelve. Monday morning you posted "DipLipGator out." Correct. Thanks for the players, dumbass.

Now **AllBidness**, you lucky shitbird. In the chop seat after the 4:25 games at 53.9 with two players left, and only 1.48 above a corpse after Sunday night. Then Dak Prescott dropped 29.28 on Monday and hauled your ass out of the grave. That's not management, that's falling off a roof and landing in a pool. **CodyPowers28** held the seat after the 1:00 and 4:05 games, at 27.28 and 31.18, posted a "So long friends" reverse jinx, and climbed to 101.68. And this part physically hurts: **joefanelli90** finished 11th at 89.02 on purpose. Sitting 5.3 clear of a finished DipLipGator, joefanelli90 left RB and TE empty instead of playing Dallas Goedert, Javonte Williams or Dameon Pierce on Monday night. An empty slot can't go negative. That's a lock-in, and it's the smartest fucking move anybody not named me made all week.

And the $25 goes to... me. Again. **avobttam**, The Executioner, 135.48 on a 133.58 projection, and I was finished before the 4:05 games even kicked off. Joe Burrow's 36.88 was the best start in the whole goddamn league, Tee Higgins added 26.8, and I put up 116.48 in the 1:00 window alone. Then I sat back and watched you animals sweat. One ring, 2024, and now back-to-back weekly checks. Legacy. **Bustersx8** chased me all weekend off Drake Maye's 31.44 on Thursday night and finished second at 133.14, 2.34 short. Close. Second pays nothing, you son of a bitch.

1.headline: Nick Merkel dropped 174.22. Jon Carter got 39.66 from Josh Allen and still finished last.
paragraphs: The compliment goes to **Nick Merkel**: 174.22, the best score in the league and 40.38 over projection even after Sleeper's bias. Dallas Goedert turned a 9.96 projection into 23.7 and Chris Olave added 28.2. The cruelty is who he played. **Mitch Pletcher** got 41.26 from Caleb Williams, scored 145.96, the highest losing score of the week, and is 0-1 because Jordan Addison gave him 0.0.

The roast goes to **Jon Carter**, who got the second-best quarterback game in the league (Josh Allen, 39.66) and turned it into the worst score in the league (93.56), 34.4 under projection. The trick was starting *two* zeros, Romeo Doubs and Colston Loveland. Chris Bova beat him while underperforming his own projection, which is the fantasy version of losing a race to a guy who stopped to tie his shoe.

And the only trade of the week already has two losers. **Austin Hendrickson** got Brock Purdy and benched him for Jared Goff, leaving 28.1 on the bench, but won anyway. **Jake Bogardus** got Mark Andrews, started him (8.9) over Kyle Monangai (20.4), started Kyle Pitts for a 0.0, and left 34.42 on the bench, the most in the league, in a 157.8 to 116.86 loss to Matt Bova.

2.headline: Jon Carter got 46.82 from Josh Allen and lost again. The commissioner got 171.76 and didn't.
paragraphs: The compliment goes to **Matt Bova**: 171.76, the best score in the league and 41.27 over projection, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba turning a 19.51 projection into 42.5 and Dak Prescott adding 37.76. Jack Hawkins benched Patrick Mahomes (34.98) for Joe Burrow (20.18) and it didn't matter; he lost by 42.28. Matt is 2-0 and leads the league in points.

The roast goes to **Jon Carter**, again. Josh Allen scored 46.82, the best starter in the league, and Jon lost 137.58 to 119.52, because Colston Loveland followed last week's zero with 1.3 and J.K. Dobbins added 3.6. That's 86.48 from Allen in two weeks and an 0-2 record. **Austin Hendrickson** benched Brock Purdy for Jared Goff again, and this time Goff won it with 37.78.

**Mitch Pletcher** played the only game of the week decided on the bench: Matthew Stafford's 35.98 sat while Caleb Williams scored 8.72, and he lost to **Mitch Blackwell** by 11.2. Blackwell started Drake Maye (9.02) over Tyler Shough (24.38) and is somehow 2-0. **Nick Merkel** got 3.0 from Saquon Barkley, -0.1 from DJ Moore and 1.4 from Dallas Goedert with George Kittle's 18.0 on the bench, and lost to Chris Bova by 41.48. And Jake Bogardus beat Chris Merkel 81.0 to 69.2 in a game nobody should watch again.

3.headline: Austin Hendrickson benched Brock Purdy for a third straight week. This time the 39.28 on his bench cost him the game.
paragraphs: The roast goes to **Austin Hendrickson**, who has earned it three weeks running. Jared Goff started at quarterback again and scored 23.36; Brock Purdy scored 39.28 on the bench. That is 99.86 from Purdy on the bench in three weeks. Add Juwan Johnson's 23.3 sitting behind Rhamondre Stevenson's 6.8, plus Luther Burden's 19.8, and Austin left 47.22 on the bench, the most in the league, in a 31.76-point loss to **Nick Merkel**. His best lineup wins that game by 15.46.

The compliment goes to **Mitch Blackwell**, who started Drake Maye over Tyler Shough for two weeks and finally flipped it. Shough scored 32.8, Harold Fannin turned a 9.46 projection into 24.1, Keenan Allen added 18.3, and Mitch beat **Chris Bova** by 43.18, 24.33 over projection net of the week's bias. He is 3-0. Chris picked up Kirk Cousins and got 28.22 from him, then 1.7 from De'Von Achane and 1.6 from Khalil Shakir with Jakobi Meyers' 19.4 on the bench.

**Matt Bova** posted the league's best score for the second straight week, 179.9, 40.39 over projection net of bias, on 35.36 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He also picked up Sam Darnold and left his 36.66 on the bench behind Dak Prescott's 20.94, which only stays funny at 3-0. **Jon Carter** is 0-3 after 85.66, the week's low, and **Andrew Evans** rode Jahmyr Gibbs' 41.4 to 3-0 as well.

4.headline: Nick Merkel started Saquon Barkley over Brian Robinson, got 2.0 instead of 25.7, and lost by 5.4.
paragraphs: The roast goes to **Nick Merkel**, who had the game won on his bench. Saquon Barkley started at flex and scored 2.0. Brian Robinson sat behind him and scored 25.7. That one swap was worth 23.7 points, and Nick lost to **Jon Carter** 137.02 to 131.62. DJ Moore added 2.7 on a 13.86 projection, Javonte Williams' 31.3 went to waste, and Nick left 33.6 on the bench in all. He is 2-2. Jon gets his first win on Nico Collins' 30.8 and 23.8 from Romeo Doubs, projected for 9.0.

The compliment goes to **Katie Bogardus**, who put up the week's best score, 166.48, 41.61 over projection net of the week's 10.07 bias. Tetairoa McMillan scored 45.2 on a 15.87 projection and CeeDee Lamb scored 41.3 on 17.42, the two best starts in the league, and she left only 9.4 on her bench. She beat **Jake Bogardus** by 41.0 for her first win. Jake started Ladd McConkey, whom Sleeper projected for 0.0, and got 0.0.

**Matt Bova** is 4-0 after the week's luckiest win: 125.7, 31.38 under projection net of bias, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 12.6 on a 22.54 projection. **Mitch Pletcher** made that look good with 79.08, the week's low, 58.43 under net, and is 0-4. **Mitch Blackwell** is also 4-0 after beating **Austin Hendrickson** 154.44 to 139.02, although he stuck with Tyler Shough, who scored 17.94, while Drake Maye scored 33.16 on his bench. **Jack Hawkins** left 41.82 on the bench, the most in the league, and lost 159.98 to 92.6 to **Chris Merkel**.

5.headline: Nick Merkel benched Brian Robinson's 25.7 last week. This week he started him, got 1.6, and lost by 1.54.
paragraphs: The roast goes to **Nick Merkel**, who has now been wrong about Brian Robinson in both directions. Last week Robinson scored 25.7 on the bench. This week Nick started him at flex, got 1.6, and left Woody Marks' 12.5 on the bench, a swap worth 10.9 in a 123.32 to 121.78 loss to **Chris Merkel**. **Jon Carter** did it bigger: J.K. Dobbins' 15.4 sat behind KC Concepcion's 1.5, he left 28.3 on the bench, the most in the league, and lost to **Mitch Blackwell** by 2.96.

The compliment goes to **Jack Hawkins**: 167.3, 45.22 over projection net of the week's 7.35 bias, and 0.0 left on his bench. Isaiah Likely turned an 11.41 projection into 32.4 and Joe Burrow added 32.6 in a 76.26-point win over **Katie Bogardus**. **Matt Bova** had the week's best score again, 182.34, 50.02 over net, on Jaylen Warren's 36.8 and Christian Watson's 32.3, and beat Chris Bova by 75.72. **Austin Hendrickson** finally saw Jared Goff over Brock Purdy pay off, 34.94 to 21.16, scored 162.54, and lost to **Andrew Evans** by 3.52 anyway.

Power rankings: Matt is No. 1 again at 5-0 with a 46-9 all-play record. The biggest fall belongs to Mitch Blackwell, down three to sixth while 5-0. His all-play is 31-24, and his record is 2.2 wins better than his scores. Austin climbed two spots to third at 2-3 behind a 36-19 all-play. The first playoff odds, from 10,000 simulated seasons built on Sleeper's projections with a random swing on every game, give Matt a 97.7% shot at the playoffs. The title favorite is Andrew at 24.0%, ahead of Matt's 21.4%. Nick is 2-3 and still at 75.2%.

6.headline: Mitch Blackwell started a 0.0 at flex over Kamara's 14.9 and lost by 1.6. Your Commish is 6-0. You're welcome.
paragraphs: Six and fucking oh. Top score in the league again, 136.32, and I beat **Austin Hendrickson** by 37.76. Fine, Dak scored 15.02 on a 22.87 projection and I finished 6.98 under net of Sleeper's bias. That's on Dak and Sleeper, not on your king. Now, **Mitch Blackwell**, you dumbass. You started Efton Chism at flex, projected for 4.43, and he scored a goddamn 0.0 while Alvin Kamara put 14.9 on your bench. You also sat Tyler Shough's 32.96 for Drake Maye's 29.8. You lost to **Nick Merkel** by 1.6. Either move alone wins it. First loss of your season, gift-wrapped by your own fingers. **Andrew Evans** benched Tre Tucker's 26.7 for Jaylen Waddle's 6.4 and lost by 23.96. Jackasses, both of you.

This next part hurts me physically. **Mitch Pletcher** got his first win: 112.48, 21.5 over projection net of bias, 0.0 left on the bench, two zeros in the lineup, and a 10.7-point win over **Jack Hawkins**. Germie Bernard turned a 9.96 projection into 25.7, and Ryan Flournoy, a free-agent pickup, scored 17.0. That is real management, you son of a bitch. I do it every week.

Power rankings: me at No. 1, obviously, at 57-9 all-play. The biggest move is **Chris Merkel**, down three to 10th after a 98.98 that came in 33.66 under projection net of bias. Blackwell lost and still climbed two to fourth, but his 39-27 all-play says his 5-1 is 1.5 wins of pure horseshit luck. Austin is 2-4 against a 36-30 all-play, 1.3 wins unlucky. The playoff odds, 10,000 simulated seasons built on Sleeper's projections with a random swing on every game, are held back this week: the simulated weekly swings ran 25.4% to 28.4%, over the 28% limit. The math choked. I didn't.

7.headline: A guy with no team name beat your Commish by 3.1. Mitch Pletcher started his own waiver pickup over 19.1 on the bench and lost by 3.4.
paragraphs: Fine. I lost. 132.88 to 135.98, by 3.1, to **Jon Carter**. Kenneth Walker turned a 19.38 projection into 9.7, Christian Watson gave me 10.7 on 17.99, and I left 0.0 on my bench. Perfect lineup, betrayed by the help. Still 6-1, still the most points in the league. Sit down. Now, **Mitch Pletcher**, you dumbass. You picked up Roschon Johnson this week and started him at RB. He scored 1.3. Cam Skattebo sat on your bench and scored 19.1. That swap is worth 17.8, you lost to **Katie Bogardus** by 3.4, and you left 24.7 on the bench, the most in the league. You're 1-6 and your waiver claim stinks like a dead fish.

And speaking of shit management. **Austin Hendrickson**, **Jon Carter**, **Mitch Pletcher**: I called all three of you out in the chat yesterday, and Sleeper still shows nothing under team name for any of you. Seven weeks. Not even a fucking team name. The compliment, and it physically hurts: **Jack Hawkins** put up the week's best score, 156.48, 20.22 over projection net of Sleeper's bias, and beat Chris Bova by 53.08. Tony Pollard turned 14.76 projected into 36.5, and Makai Lemon, a pickup off the wire this week, scored 19.7. That's real management. I would know.

Power rankings: me at No. 1, obviously, at 64-13 all-play. Jack and Jon each climbed two, to fourth and seventh. **Mitch Blackwell** fell two to sixth while 6-1: his 44-33 all-play says 2.0 of those wins are horseshit luck. **Nick Merkel** is third at 3-4, 1.8 wins unlucky. The playoff odds, 10,000 simulated seasons built on Sleeper's projections with a random swing on every game, are held back again: the simulated weekly swings ran 25.6% to 28.7%, over the 28% limit.

1.headline: All 18 picked the Chargers. djbogardus72 took the $20 by guessing Monday night within two points.
paragraphs: Week 1 in one number: **18 for 18** on the Chargers, an 80% favorite, and Arizona won 26-14. Everybody also took Detroit, which survived New Orleans 31-30 and saved the entire league from a very long Monday. Four favorites went down in total, and nobody in the league picked a single one of the upsets.

So nobody won the week by being different. There was not one lonely win in the pool. **CHRISMERKELDUH**, **djbogardus72** and **NastyNate725** went 7-1 as the only three who stayed off all three of the other traps: the Rams (10 took them, San Francisco won 27-7), the Cowboys (8 took them, the Giants won 28-20) and the Titans (2 took them, the Jets won 23-10). That sent it to the tiebreaker, and Denver and Kansas City combined for 41. **djbogardus72** said 43 and takes the $20. NastyNate725 said 37. CHRISMERKELDUH said 48 and gets nothing for a perfect-except-the-Chargers week. Every 6-2 entry stepped on exactly one trap, commissioner **avobttam** and his Sunday-night Dallas pick included.

Last place is **Bustersx8** at 4-4, who managed to find the Rams, the Titans *and* the Chargers, then went solo on Green Bay as the only person in the league to pick the Packers. Minnesota won 39-22. Being different only pays when you are also right.

2.headline: Four favorites fell and nobody in the league picked a single upset. cbova1222 dodged three of the four and takes the $20 outright.
paragraphs: Week 2 was a minefield and the whole league walked into it together. Baltimore (77%, 16 of 18 took them) lost 24-17 to New Orleans. Tampa Bay (78%, 16 of 18) lost 23-19 to Cleveland. Chicago (66%, 10 takers) scored three points against Minnesota. The Chargers (73%, 9 takers) lost 26-14 to Las Vegas. Four upsets, zero people on the right side of any of them, and for the second week running not one lonely win in the pool.

So the $20 went to the one entry that stepped around the most holes. **cbova1222** went 7-1, the only 7 in the league, no tiebreaker needed. The only miss was Baltimore, which nearly everybody missed. They stayed off Tampa, Chicago and the Chargers, and were one of just three on Buffalo and one of two on Dallas. That is not being different. That is being right about which chalk was rotten, and it pays the same. Season leaders **CHRISMERKELDUH** and **djbogardus72** both went 6-2 on the Ravens and Bucs and sit on 13, with cbova1222 one back in a four-way tie at 12.

Four entries went 4-4. Commissioner **avobttam**, **katiestout13** and **Kolisekj52** each collected all four losing favorites, a perfect record of wrong. **MJBlack** found three of them and then went solo on Arizona, the only Cardinals pick in the league. Seattle won 31-7. Kolisekj52 is now last for the season at 9.

3.headline: Seven favorites fell. bjander110 went alone on Las Vegas and takes the $20 with six right.
paragraphs: Week 3 was worse than week 2. Seven favorites lost, and the whole league found three correct upset picks between them. Seattle (76%, 17 of 18 took them) lost 33-31 in Washington. Philadelphia (64%, 15 takers) scored seven points in Chicago on Monday night. Green Bay (69%, 14 takers) lost 35-14 to Atlanta on Thursday night, which wrecked most cards before Sunday. Cincinnati (62%, 11 takers) lost 30-27 in Pittsburgh, and all six Carolina backers watched Cleveland win 21-18.

The $20 goes to **bjander110**, outright, no tiebreaker: 6-1, the only six in the pool, on seven picks instead of eight. They stayed off Green Bay, Philadelphia and Cincinnati, and were the only entry in the league on Las Vegas, a 38% underdog that won 35-27 in New Orleans. That lonely win is the whole margin. **Bogeyman28** and **AngryWillis** were the only two on Indianapolis, and five entries finished 5-3. **CHRISMERKELDUH** leads the season on 18, one clear of bjander110 and **djbogardus72**.

At the bottom, two entries went alone on a road underdog in the 1:00 window and got buried for it. **NickBova** took New England, beaten 35-6 in Jacksonville, and went 2-5. **steveedwards** took Tennessee, went 2-6, and is last for the season on 12. Commissioner **avobttam** went 4-4 on Green Bay, Carolina, Seattle and Philadelphia, four favorites and four losses, and sits at 14.

4.headline: Seven more favorites fell and nobody had a lonely win. NickBova and camschnick went 7-1, and the Monday night total gave NickBova the $20.
paragraphs: Week 4 matched week 3 with seven upsets, and the league did not get one of the big ones right. Buffalo (73%, 15 of 18 took them) lost 29-26 to New England. Detroit (65%, 13 takers) lost 32-26 in Carolina on Sunday night. Pittsburgh (59%, five takers) lost 27-24 in Cleveland on Thursday, and the three entries on New Orleans watched Atlanta score 45 on Monday night. Nobody picked New England, Carolina, Cleveland or Atlanta. The only correct upset picks were the Giants, Dallas and Jacksonville, two entries each, so nobody had a lonely win this week.

That left a tie at 7-1 between **camschnick**, whose miss was Buffalo, and **NickBova**, whose miss was Pittsburgh on Thursday and who was one of the two on Dallas, 34-30 winners in Houston. The $20 is never split, so it went to the tiebreaker. Atlanta and New Orleans scored 69. NickBova guessed 52, 17 off. camschnick guessed 45, 24 off. The $20 goes to **NickBova**, one week after going 2-5. camschnick, **CHRISMERKELDUH** and **djbogardus72** share the season lead on 23.

At the bottom, commissioner **avobttam** went 4-4 for the second straight week, this time on Arizona, Buffalo, Detroit and New Orleans, and is 18 for the season. **MJBlack** also went 4-4 and is also on 18. **steveedwards** went 5-3, missing on Buffalo, Detroit and New Orleans, and is last on 17.

5.headline: Seven entries went 7-1. steveedwards guessed the Monday night total at exactly 71 and takes the $20.
paragraphs: Week 5 was decided on Thursday night for most of the league. Dallas, an 80% favorite and the pick of 13 of 18 entries, lost 24-16 to Tampa Bay. Four more favorites fell: Chicago scored seven in Green Bay, San Francisco won 32-29 in Seattle, Baltimore won 30-23 in Atlanta, and Buffalo beat the Rams 37-34 on Monday night, with four of the five entries in that game on the Bills. The five on Washington got nothing either way: the Giants and Commanders tied 27-27.

Seven entries finished 7-1: **bjander110**, **Bogeyman28**, **camschnick**, **CHRISMERKELDUH**, **msymons713**, **NickBova** and **steveedwards**. **Bogeyman28** had the only lonely wins in the pool, the only Green Bay pick and the only Jets pick, which is exactly how the $20 is supposed to be won. It wasn't. The $20 is never split, so it went to the tiebreaker, and Buffalo and the Rams scored 71. Bogeyman28 guessed 42, the furthest off of the seven. **steveedwards** guessed 71, dead on, and takes the $20. bjander110 and NickBova said 56. **camschnick** and **CHRISMERKELDUH** share the season lead on 30.

At the bottom, **katiestout13** went 3-4 with a push, on Dallas, Cleveland, Las Vegas and New Orleans, the worst card of the week. Commissioner **avobttam** went 6-2 on Dallas and Indianapolis and sits on 24 for the season, in a four-way tie for last with katiestout13, **MJBlack** and steveedwards. One of the four just won the $20.

6.headline: Seventeen of 18 took the Rams, and Arizona won 18-16. Four went 6-2, and bjander110 guessed the Monday night total within one to take the $20.
paragraphs: Five favorites lost, and not one entry picked any of the five underdogs that beat them. The big one was Arizona 18, Rams 16: the Rams were an 86% favorite and the pick of 17 of 18 entries. Tennessee won 26-20 in Indianapolis with 15 entries on the Colts. Cleveland beat Baltimore 13-10 with eight on the Ravens, Houston won 34-31 in Jacksonville with seven on the Jaguars, and Denver beat Seattle 17-14 with two on the Seahawks.

That left a four-way tie at 6-2: **AngryWillis**, **bjander110**, **djbogardus72** and commissioner **avobttam**, all four undone by the Colts and the Rams. The only lonely win in the pool was **Bogeyman28**'s, the lone New Orleans pick, on a 3-5 card. The $20 is never split, so it went to the tiebreaker, and Washington and San Francisco scored 40 on Monday night. **bjander110** guessed 41 and takes the $20. AngryWillis said 44, djbogardus72 56, and avobttam 59, the furthest off of the four.

bjander110, **camschnick** and djbogardus72 share the season lead on 35, with **CHRISMERKELDUH** a point back. **NickBova** submitted two picks, went 2-0, and finished last for the week. avobttam sits on 30, five back of the lead.

7.headline: Houston, the Jets, San Francisco and Carolina all lost. AngryWillis went 6 for 8 and takes the $20 alone.
paragraphs: Four favorites went down and took 44 picks with them. Houston, an 80% favorite, lost 27-21 to the Giants with all 15 of its pickers aboard. The Jets lost 28-25 to Miami with 12, San Francisco lost in Atlanta with 10, and Carolina lost 43-13 to Tampa Bay with 7 of its 8. Not one entry picked the Giants, the Dolphins or the Falcons.

**AngryWillis** went 6 for 8, the only entry to get to six, and takes the $20 outright, no tiebreaker needed. There was no lonely win in it. The edge was simply staying off San Francisco and Carolina, which every other entry that made eight picks failed to do. The only lonely wins belonged to **steveedwards**, alone on Tampa Bay, and **Mpletcher**, alone on Chicago. **MJBlack** went a perfect 5 for 5 and left three picks unmade, which is a clean sheet and one win short of $20.

At the bottom, **Bogeyman28** went 3 for 8 on Green Bay, Las Vegas, San Francisco, Houston and the Jets, and **NickBova** matched it. **katiestout13** and **NastyNate725** also finished on three, from five picks each. Commissioner **avobttam** took Carolina, Houston and the Jets and went 5 for 8. On the season, **bjander110** and **djbogardus72** share the lead at 40, one ahead of **camschnick** and **CHRISMERKELDUH**, and the week moves AngryWillis up to 37.

1.headline: Seven people rode the Chargers in survivor. Arizona handed out seven strikes.
paragraphs: Nobody is dead yet, and that is the only good news. With two revives each, all 20 entries are still standing, but **8 of 20 burned a life in week 1**. The pick that did it was the Chargers, an 80% favorite and tied for the most popular pick in the pool with seven takers, who lost to Arizona 26-14. Strikes for **bjander110**, **Bustersx8**, **camschnick**, **CHRISMERKELDUH**, **JellyRoll6884**, **MerkDaddy36** and **NastyNate725**.

The eighth strike was a solo job. **MJBlack** went with Tennessee, a 52% coin flip that nobody else in the pool touched, and the Jets won 23-10. Going contrarian in survivor is a strategy. Going contrarian on a coin flip in week 1 is a donation.

The other half of the chalk carried everyone else. The seven on Jacksonville cruised, 34-10 over Cleveland. Pittsburgh (20-13) and Chicago (59-37) held up for their takers, and the two on Detroit, **AngryWillis** and **Kolisekj52**, sweated out a 31-30 win over New Orleans. Twelve clean, eight on one strike, zero bodies. Yet.

2.headline: Half the pool rode Tampa Bay. Cleveland handed out ten strikes, and six entries are now down to their last life.
paragraphs: Still no bodies, but the pool is bleeding. **10 of 20 entries took Tampa Bay**, a 78% favorite, and Cleveland won 23-19. Every one of them took a strike: **AllBidness**, **Cubbiesftw23**, **djbogardus72**, **katiestout13**, **Kolisekj52** and **woody1108** burn their first life, while **camschnick**, **MJBlack**, **NastyNate725** and **bjander110** burn their second. When half the league agrees on a pick in survivor, the upside is safety in numbers. The downside is exactly this.

Then there are the two who took a strike without having to watch. **Bustersx8** and **JellyRoll6884** submitted no pick, which costs a life all the same, and both are now on two strikes. Losing on a 78% favorite is bad luck. Losing on no pick at all is a choice.

The other ten walked through clean. The three on San Francisco, including commissioner **avobttam**, cruised 35-13 over Miami. The three on Philadelphia sweated out a 24-20 win at Tennessee, and **cbova1222** rode Kansas City to a 33-30 escape. Six entries are still strike-free, eight are on one, and six have one life left going into week 3. The first body is coming.

3.headline: Six bodies in Deadpool, and five of them never turned in a pick. camschnick at least went down swinging on Seattle.
paragraphs: The first bodies arrived all at once. Six entries went into week 3 on their last life, and all six are gone. Only **camschnick** actually lost a game: Seattle, a 76% favorite, blew it 33-31 in Washington, and camschnick was the only entry on them. The other five, **Bustersx8**, **JellyRoll6884**, **MJBlack**, **NastyNate725** and **bjander110**, submitted no pick at all, and a missing pick on your last life is a death like any other. bjander110 won the $20 in Infinity War this week on a lonely Las Vegas pick and could not find one team to pick here.

The living mostly played it safe. Seven of the 15 picks went to Kansas City, an 83% favorite that won 24-10 in Miami, and four more rode Detroit past the Jets. The two who strayed paid for it. **Kolisekj52** took Green Bay on Thursday night, lost 35-14 to Atlanta, and is on two strikes. **KeithWaters**, strike-free for two weeks, took Philadelphia and watched Chicago win 27-7 on Monday night. **cbova1222** went alone on San Francisco and survived 36-30.
Fourteen are left. Five are still perfect, including commissioner **avobttam** on Kansas City, eight are on one strike, and Kolisekj52 is the only entry down to a last life.

4.headline: Fourteen picks, fourteen wins. Nobody died in Deadpool, and seven entries survived a 15-10 Minnesota win.
paragraphs: The first clean week of the season. All 14 living entries made a pick and all 14 won. Seven favorites lost in week 4, including Buffalo, Detroit and Pittsburgh, and not one of them was on a Deadpool card. Seven entries took Minnesota, an 82% favorite that held off Miami 15-10 at 4:05. Five took Baltimore, an 85% favorite that beat Tennessee 24-18. **NickBova** went alone on Indianapolis, 30-13 winners in Washington in the 9:30 game, and **KeithWaters** went alone on Seattle, 30-23 over the Chargers.

**Kolisekj52**, the only entry on a last life, took Baltimore and survived the 24-18. Fourteen of 20 are still alive. Five are still perfect: **AngryWillis**, **cbova1222**, **Mpletcher**, **NickBova** and commissioner **avobttam**, who rode Minnesota. Eight are on one strike, and Kolisekj52 is still the only one down to a last life.

5.headline: Nine of 14 rode Dallas. Tampa Bay won 24-16 on Thursday night, handed out eight strikes, and finished off Kolisekj52.
paragraphs: The consensus pick got the whole consensus. **9 of the 14 living entries took Dallas**, an 80% favorite, and Tampa Bay won 24-16 on Thursday night, so nine cards were dead before Sunday. **Kolisekj52**, on a last life since week 3, took Dallas and is the first body since then. Seven more burn their second life and are now one loss from done: **AllBidness**, **CHRISMERKELDUH**, **djbogardus72**, **katiestout13**, **KeithWaters**, **MerkDaddy36** and **woody1108**. Commissioner **avobttam** took Dallas too and loses a perfect record, the first strike in five weeks.

The five who looked elsewhere had a quiet Sunday. **AngryWillis**, **cbova1222**, **Cubbiesftw23** and **NickBova** took Cincinnati, 31-24 winners in Miami, and **Mpletcher** went alone on Houston, 26-3 in Tennessee.

Thirteen of 20 are still alive. Four are still perfect: AngryWillis, cbova1222, Mpletcher and NickBova. avobttam and Cubbiesftw23 are on one strike, and seven entries are now on a last life, up from one a week ago.

6.headline: Four took the Colts and Tennessee won 26-20. CHRISMERKELDUH died on the Rams, and five last-life entries died without making a pick.
paragraphs: Six bodies this week, and five of them never lost a game. **djbogardus72**, **katiestout13**, **KeithWaters**, **MerkDaddy36** and **woody1108** all burned a second life on Dallas in week 5, went into week 6 on a last life, and made no pick. That is how you leave a survivor pool without even the dignity of a bad pick. **CHRISMERKELDUH**, on the same last life, at least picked: the Rams, an 86% favorite, and Arizona won 18-16.

The consensus got hit again. Four of the eight who picked took Indianapolis, a 74% favorite, and Tennessee won 26-20. Commissioner **avobttam** and **Cubbiesftw23** burn their second life and are down to their last. **cbova1222** and **Mpletcher** had been perfect and take a first strike. The commissioner has now taken a strike on the consensus pick two weeks running.

**AngryWillis** and **AllBidness** took New England, 26-19 over the Jets, and **NickBova** went alone on San Francisco, 23-17 over Washington. Seven of 20 are left. AngryWillis and NickBova are still perfect, cbova1222 and Mpletcher are on one strike, and AllBidness, avobttam and Cubbiesftw23 are on a last life.

7.headline: Houston was an 80% favorite and five of the last seven took it. The Giants won 27-21 and Deadpool is down to four.
paragraphs: Seven went in, four came out, and Houston did nearly all of it. The Texans were an 80% favorite at home against the Giants, five of the seven entries still standing took them, and New York won 27-21. That was a third strike and the end for **avobttam**, **AllBidness** and **Cubbiesftw23**. Yes, the commissioner is dead, killed by the consensus pick like everybody else who trusted it.

Two more Houston pickers live on strikes: **NickBova** takes a first and **cbova1222** a second. **Mpletcher** went off the board with Carolina, which was at least different, and Carolina lost 43-13 to Tampa Bay for a second strike. Going contrarian works better when the contrarian pick shows up.

The only correct pick of the week belonged to **AngryWillis**, alone on Denver, which won in Arizona. AngryWillis is the only one of the four left without a strike. The other three carry five between them.

2.headline: Three favorites fell and eleven entries took a strike. The 13 on San Francisco never broke a sweat.
paragraphs: Nobody died, but week 2 took a bite out of the pool. Eleven of 31 entries lost their pick, spread across three upsets. Tampa Bay, a 78% favorite, lost 23-19 to Cleveland and took six with them: **AJPeak**, **domfan**, **leftypapa**, **lisaseidl**, **MichaelSeidl** and **SaraWuite**. Baltimore, 77%, lost 24-17 to New Orleans and took four: **AFrange**, **cbova1222**, **NickBova** and **Perko87**. **vcaval** went alone on the Chargers, the only entry in the pool on them, and Las Vegas won 26-14.

The consensus was the smart money. **13 entries took San Francisco**, an 88% favorite and the safest pick on the board, and the 49ers beat Miami 35-13. Commissioner **avobttam** was one of them, which stops the bleeding after a week 1 strike rather than undoing it.

Two entries took a strike without picking anything. **CBrown59** and **TonyGuazu** submitted no pick and are now on two strikes, one away from done, alongside **SaraWuite**, whose Tampa pick was the second strike. Ten entries are still perfect, eighteen are on one strike, and three are on their last life. For those three, week 3 is the first week a loss can end it.

3.headline: Poop has its first two bodies, and neither one made a pick. Fourteen rode Kansas City and walked through.
paragraphs: The first bodies are in, and neither one lost a game. **CBrown59** and **TonyGuazu** went into week 3 on two strikes after skipping week 2, skipped again, and are out. **SaraWuite**, the third entry on a last life, took San Francisco and survived 36-30. Twenty-nine of 31 are still standing.

Fourteen entries took Kansas City, an 83% favorite, and the Chiefs won 24-10 in Miami. Six of the fourteen who looked elsewhere found an upset instead. **DunkinDutchman45** and **aelliott2214** took Green Bay on Thursday night and lost 35-14 to Atlanta. **markymark317** and **NickBova** took New Orleans, and Las Vegas won 35-27. **jj833041** took Philadelphia into Chicago on Monday night and lost 27-7, and **vcaval**, the only Seattle pick in the pool, lost 33-31 in Washington. That is two weeks running vcaval has been the only entry on a losing team.

**cbova1222** submitted no pick and takes a second strike for it, joining **NickBova**, **vcaval** and **SaraWuite** on a last life. Commissioner **avobttam** rode Kansas City and stays on one strike, one of 19 entries there. Six are still perfect.

4.headline: Nobody lost a game in Poop, and two entries died anyway. cbova1222 and vcaval went into week 4 on a last life and never made a pick.
paragraphs: Two more bodies, and once again neither one lost a game. **cbova1222** took a second strike in week 3 for skipping a pick, and **vcaval** took one for being the only entry on Seattle. Both went into week 4 on a last life, both submitted no pick, and both are out. Twenty-seven of 31 are still standing.

Everybody who did pick won: 26 picks, 26 wins. Seventeen entries took Minnesota, an 82% favorite that beat Miami 15-10, and seven took Baltimore, 24-18 over Tennessee. **Perko87** went alone on Seattle, 30-23 over the Chargers, and **AFrange** went alone on Kansas City and sweated out a 30-27 win in Las Vegas. **NickBova** and **SaraWuite**, both on a last life, took Minnesota and survived a five-point game.

**markymark317** submitted no pick and takes a second strike for it, joining NickBova and SaraWuite on a last life. Commissioner **avobttam** took Baltimore and stays on one strike, one of 18 entries there. Six are still perfect.

5.headline: Six rode Dallas into a Thursday night loss and took strikes. The only body was markymark317, who skipped a pick on a last life.
paragraphs: One more body, and like all four before it, it never lost a game. **markymark317** skipped week 4 for a second strike, went into week 5 on a last life, skipped again, and is out. Twenty-six of 31 are still standing.

The strikes all came from one game. Dallas, an 80% favorite, lost 24-16 to Tampa Bay on Thursday night, and six entries went down with it. **AJPeak**, **Perko87**, **stuto**, **Yungmulletgoat** and commissioner **avobttam** burn their second life and are now on their last. **Isabelle312** had been perfect and takes a first strike. The commissioner also took Dallas in Deadpool, so one bad Thursday cost two lives.

Everyone else won. Twelve entries took Houston, the consensus pick, 26-3 winners in Tennessee. Five took Cincinnati, 31-24 in Miami, **aelliott2214** and **DunkinDutchman45** took Detroit, 45-21 in Arizona, and **sydguthrie** went alone on Pittsburgh, 34-22 over Indianapolis. **NickBova** and **SaraWuite**, both on a last life, survived on Cincinnati and Houston. Five are still perfect, fourteen are on one strike, and seven are on a last life.

6.headline: Twenty of 25 picks lost on the Rams and the Colts. Five died, avobttam among them, and Yungmulletgoat went out without a pick.
paragraphs: Week 6 was a massacre. Twelve entries took the Rams, an 86% favorite, and Arizona won 18-16. Eight took the Colts, and Tennessee won 26-20 in Indianapolis. That is 20 losses from 25 picks, and all five perfect entries took a first strike: **albuchan**, **CarlosDangers** and **sydguthrie** on the Rams, **Intipach** and **JohnDaveyNATTYCHAMP** on the Colts.

Five went out on a last life: **AJPeak**, **SaraWuite** and **stuto** on the Colts, **Perko87** and commissioner **avobttam** on the Rams. That is both of the commissioner's survivor entries beaten in one week, and this one is over. **Yungmulletgoat** made no pick on a last life and is the sixth body. Ten more burn a second life: **aelliott2214**, **DunkinDutchman45**, **Elworth**, **glizzygladiator25**, **Isabelle312**, **joefanelli90** and **KyliePeacock** on the Rams, **leftypapa**, **lisaseidl** and **MichaelSeidl** on the Colts.

Five picks won. **AFrange**, **domfan** and **jj833041** took New England, 26-19 over the Jets, **creckley** went alone on Kansas City, 22-6 over the Chargers, and **NickBova**, on a last life, went alone on San Francisco. Twenty of 31 are alive. Nobody is perfect anymore: nine are on one strike and eleven are on a last life.

7.headline: The Jets, Houston and Carolina all lost in the 1:00 window. Poop lost five and is down to fifteen.
paragraphs: Twenty went in, fifteen came out, and three upsets in the 1:00 window did it. The Jets were the joint consensus pick with four entries and lost 28-25 to Miami: **KyliePeacock** and **glizzygladiator25** are out on a third strike, and **Intipach** and **JohnDaveyNATTYCHAMP** survive on a second. Houston, an 80% favorite, lost 27-21 to the Giants: **joefanelli90** and **DunkinDutchman45** are dead and **albuchan** takes a second strike. **lisaseidl** went alone on Carolina, which lost 43-13 to Tampa Bay, and that was strike three.

Minnesota shared the consensus with the Jets at four entries and won, which was the entire difference between those eight this week. **NickBova** went alone on Cleveland and got the week's only lonely win. Eight of twenty lost a pick, five of them for good.
Nobody left has a clean record. Six of the fifteen carry one strike and nine are on their last life.
